Audit log export schema and retention/rotation

SOC2 readiness and evidence capture plan

transcript:
[00:00] Avery (AE): All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. We are at 15:00 UTC, looks like about 47 minutes on the calendar. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Samira (Velocis sec): Samira here, Samira Khan. Sorry, had an onboarding call run a bit late.
[00:12] Tom (Velocis infra): Tom Bell on platform infra.
[00:14] Nina (Velocis PM): Nina Patel, product.
[00:16] Miguel (Redwood SE): Miguel Ortiz, SE. Good to see you all.
[00:19] Avery: Cool. Main agenda today is SSO check, audit log export format, data retention numbers and then quick SOC2 evidence ask. Anything to add?
[00:28] Samira: No, that's perfect. We're mainly trying to figure out how Redwood's logs will fit into our SIEM and what exactly you'll keep in the hosted pilot.
[00:36] Miguel: Great. I'll share my screen — okay, can everyone see my screen? (minor audio)
[00:42] Nina: Yes. Looks good.
[00:44] Miguel: So first thing, SAML config. We have a standard metadata blob, you can upload it in the console or we can do IdP-initiated. Note there are two important attributes we pass: email and roles.
[00:58] Samira: Quick note — in our staging IdP, the attribute is called memberOf not roles, so mapping will be necessary.
[01:06] Miguel: Yeah, we can map that; console has a mapping table. Sometimes the auto mapping gets picky — I've seen it try to match "samel" instead of SAML in logs, small transcriber quirk — but mapping is purely config.
[01:20] Avery: Also, for audit, we need to confirm what events are emitted. Miguel, can you list the key events we log?
[01:27] Miguel: Sure: auth.success, auth.failure, session.create, session.terminate, model.call.start, model.call.complete, quota.alert, config.change, key.rotate — the key rotation one is important for KMS integrations.
[01:40] Tom: For KMS — are you using customer-managed keys for the private deployment? We're planning to test KMS integration in the VPC pilot.
[01:48] Miguel: Yes, we support CMK via KMS/HSM for Private. For hosted we can do envelope encryption and we also offer bring-your-own-key for Dedicated in most regions. There can be minor skews in the event names though, e.g., key.rotate might appear as key_update in some of our older audits, Miguel chuckles.
[02:02] Samira: Ok, how do we get the logs out? We want a push to S3 or a streamed syslog into Splunk.
[02:09] Miguel: We support S3 export and webhooks; Splunk via HEC with an event forwarder is common. For the POC I can stitch together an S3 drop with partitioned prefixes: /year=2027/month=04/day=14/ and gzipped JSON.
[02:24] Nina: Do you include request/response payloads in those logs?
[02:27] Miguel: By default audit logs include metadata: request id, user id, timestamp, model name, token counts, latency, and a hashed request fingerprint. Raw prompt and response bodies are not included by default in audit exports for privacy reasons, but they can be toggled on with strict guardrails and redaction rules.
[02:45] Samira: We will need examples of the export schema, specifically the field names. Our SIEM team hates surprises.
[02:52] Miguel: Understood. I'll attach a sample JSON next. Note: there is also an opaque kv cache artifact… it's sometimes referenced as K V cache in older notes — it's the key-value token cache for streaming completions; we do not persist raw KV by default in hosted.
[03:07] Tom: Important for us — embeddings retention. We do not want raw embeddings stored beyond 7 days unless encrypted and approved. Is that configurable?
[03:14] Miguel: Embedding retention is configurable. For Hosted pilot the default is 30 days; we can change that for the pilot to 7 days. For Private/Dedicated you control retention and can disable persistent embeddings entirely.
[03:24] Avery: On SOC2, Samira, do you have a checklist of artifacts you need?
[03:28] Samira: Yes, principal asks are: access logs, change history for config and model versions, encryption usage, onboarding docs for who had access during pilot, and evidence of log retention policy. Also, an incident response flow.
[03:40] Miguel: We can provide an audit evidence bundle — includes auth audit, config change diffs, key rotation timestamps, and a tamper-evident log digest. For incident response we can map our escalation with your contacts.
[03:51] Nina: On model versions — if we pin to a specific model during pilot, can Redwood show a hash or checksum for the model binary in the logs?
[03:59] Miguel: Yes, we emit model.version and model.checksum in the model.call.start event. That helps for reproducibility.
[04:05] Tom: Network question — for Private we want egress IPs whitelisted, also whether you do NAT on our side or yours.
[04:12] Miguel: For Private we can peer into your VPC or run in your project; typically egress is in your environment so you control NAT. For Dedicated there's an option to allocate static egress IPs from our pool. I'll follow up with the exact IP ranges.
[04:28] Samira: Back to SSO — we tried a test and got a 401. Error message was "invalid audience". Any quick checks?
[04:35] Miguel: That usually means the SP entityID doesn't match the audience in the assertion. Check the app config in Okta/Azure and confirm the audience matches the SP entity we provided. Also check clock skew — SAML can fail if clocks are off by more than 2 minutes.
[04:49] Samira: Yep, clocks in staging are funky, we'll sync NTP.
[04:53] Avery: If SAML is flaky, fallback plan for team members is invite-only accounts with enforced MFA, correct?
[04:59] Miguel: Correct. We can create invite-only RBAC users and enforce org-level MFA.
[05:05] Nina: Can we restrict certain users from exporting audit logs? We don't want product folks accidentally pulling raw transcripts.
[05:12] Miguel: RBAC supports fine-grained permissions: export.logs, view.metrics, manage.users. You can restrict export.logs to an Admin role only.
[05:20] Tom: On retention again — what about chat transcripts that are stored temporarily during inference for caching? How long are those kept in the KV or prefix caches?
[05:28] Miguel: The prefix cache (for latency improvements) is in-memory on the runtime and has a sliding TTL typically 5–20 minutes depending on config. KV cache for session state can be persisted but by default is ephemeral and purged after session. We can configure a shorter TTL for pilot.
[05:42] Samira: Great. For compliance evidence we'll need a diagram showing where caches live and how they're purged.
[05:48] Miguel: I'll add that to the artifact bundle.
[05:51] Avery: Any questions about log schema — I've seen customers confuse model.call.complete and request.complete.
[05:58] Miguel: That's a good callout — model.call.complete is specific to model token generation finished; request.complete is end-to-end including middleware routing. We'll annotate them in the sample schema.
[06:10] (00:06:10) Samira: small side note, are you supporting SCIM for user provisioning?
[06:16] Miguel: Yes, SCIM is supported for Dedicated and Private, with webhooks for delta syncs. For hosted we have limited SCIM; it's typically available on enterprise plans.
[06:26] Nina: On the topic of PII redaction — can Redwood apply deterministic redaction rules pre-ingest? For example, mask ssn-like patterns and emails?
[06:35] Miguel: We have pre-ingest filters. They run as a pipeline: tokenization -> rule-based redaction -> optional ML-based NER redaction. There's a config to mask or redact-in-place. Note there can be false positives so we recommend sampling rules first.
[06:50] Tom: Any performance hit when running redaction? We're worried about latency tail.
[06:55] Miguel: Small CPU overhead for rule-based; if you run ML-based NER it adds 15–30ms median per request on our runtime. But for most text workloads it's within SLO if you provision correctly. We can give you quant numbers from the pilot.
[07:10] Samira: Ok, let's get specific — Miguel, can you give us the sample audit log entry?
[07:14] Miguel: I'll paste a simplified line: {"ts":"2027-04-14T15:02:12Z","evt":"model.call.start","uid":"u-123","model":"redwood-v1","call_id":"c-987","tokens_in":42}.
[07:28] Nina: Will the call_id map to a URL for playback?
[07:31] Miguel: call_id is the canonical key; we don't expose raw playback URLs in the export but you can query the console or API with the call_id to fetch the artifact if permitted.
[07:41] Samira: We need to ensure playback is gated and appears in the audit when someone fetches it.
[07:47] Miguel: Yes — fetch events are logged: artifact.access with user id and timestamp.
[07:52] Avery: Time check — we're about 8 minutes in. I'd like to move to the demo Miguel mentioned about exporting an audit bundle.
[08:00] Miguel: I'll trigger a sample export now — you'll get an S3 link. (typing) Sending to the chat… ok link posted. Note the export omits prompt body by default; there's a show_sensitive:true flag but it's disabled for hosted by default.
[08:20] Tom: Got the link, starting download… Hmm the file claims gzip but Chrome tried to preview it raw, so fields are a bit squashed.
[08:29] Miguel: Sorry, I should have mentioned. It's gzipped jsonl; each line is an event. I'll send an uncompressed sample too.
[08:38] Samira: Can you include a field mapping table? Things like model.call.complete -> duration_ms etc.
[08:45] Miguel: Yes, mapping table will go out. Also, I'll include translation notes because older exports used slightly different names.
[08:54] Nina: On SOC2 — do you have a SOC2 report we can see for Redwood Hosted?
[08:59] Miguel: We have a SOC2 Type II report; for Hosted we redact customer-specific details. I'll coordinate with compliance to provide an NDA'd copy.
[09:09] Samira: For the pilot we need the specific controls that map to our vendor risk assessment — if you can provide control IDs and evidence pointers, that'll speed approval.
[09:18] Miguel: Absolutely, we'll produce a control mapping doc: control id -> artifact (log path or screen recording).
[09:25] Avery: A quick risk question — in the hosted pilot if someone escalates a data deletion request, what's the workflow?
[09:32] Miguel: We have a deletion API: you supply user id or call_id, and we issue a purge across indices; deletion jobs are auditable and we return a job id in the audit log. For Hosted we also support DSR compliance; retention windows are captured in policy docs.
[09:47] Tom: How long until deletion completes? For large indices does it go async?
[09:52] Miguel: It's async. Small objects take minutes; large indices could be hours depending on size and retention tier. We return progress in the job object.
[10:03] Samira: We will want proof of deletion — a signed digest or an audit entry with tombstone.
[10:08] Miguel: We emit deletion.complete with a tombstone hash; we can include certificate signing for critical deletes on Dedicated.
[10:18] Nina: Are you able to run a short smoke test of SAML now or do we need separate window?
[10:22] Samira: We can attempt now if Miguel is ready — staging creds loaded.
[10:25] Miguel: I'm ready — Samira, if you attempt a login I'll watch logs.
[10:29] Samira: Attempting… Ok I got 401 again.
[10:32] Miguel: Checking real-time logs… I see the assertion arrived but audience is incorrect. It's expecting sp://redwood/velocis-staging but assertion has sp://velocis/app.
[10:41] Tom: Then that's on our side. We'll change the audience and retry.
[10:44] Samira: Will do.
[10:46] (00:10:46) Miguel: While they change that I'll pivot to retention metrics. For tokens we can show avg tokens per convo and retention counts. For this pilot we have the following default: token meta retained 90 days, raw transcripts 30 days, embeddings 30 days. You asked to get embeddings down to 7.
[11:02] Samira: Correct. Also need to ensure raw transcripts are redacted within 48 hours for any PII hits.
[11:07] Miguel: We can do: raw transcripts retained 48 hours then redacted, or store only redacted transcripts thereafter. We'll include sample redactions.
[11:17] Nina: Are redactions deterministic? If someone asks to unredact later for debugging, is there a reversible process?
[11:23] Miguel: Redaction is irreversible unless you store a reversible encryption envelope which requires KMS backdoors; that approach has compliance implications. We generally recommend irreversible redaction for PII.
[11:36] Samira: We prefer irreversible.
[11:38] Miguel: Good.
[11:40] Avery: Quick callout — competitor question: do you tool against Anthropic or OpenAI for latency? They asked in RFP.
[11:46] Miguel: We have internal benchmarks; for small prompts Redwood-hosted median 60ms token emission; Anthropic at parity in some tests, OpenAI sometimes faster on certain sizes. We'll share a small benchmark summary but callouts depend heavily on model and tokenization.
[12:02] Tom: Back to the SAML test: I updated the audience, Samira try again.
[12:06] Samira: Retrying… ok success, I'm in.
[12:08] Miguel: Nice. I see auth.success in real-time.
[12:10] Nina: Great. That solves the immediate SSO gating.
[12:13] Avery: Let's capture that in action items — Samira to verify team logins and report failures.
[12:18] Samira: Yep will do.
[12:20] Miguel: Next thing — evidence collection for SOC2: do you want raw logs or summarized artifacts? Usually customers want both: raw for auditors and summarized for internal review. We can produce both in the bundle.
[12:33] Samira: We'll want both, plus the control mapping.
[12:36] Miguel: Got it.
[12:38] (00:12:38) Avery: Time check — 25 minutes gone? We should move to pricing ask briefly.
[12:45] Avery: For the pilot extension, do you prefer Dedicated or Hosted for us? We know Velocis is sensitive about logs and KMS.
[12:53] Miguel: If you need CMK and full control over retention, Private or Dedicated is cleaner. Hosted can be configured with envelope keys and limited retention but Dedicated gives you isolated pools and static egress. There's a cost delta; I'll send the detailed comparison.
[13:08] Tom: How long to spin up a Dedicated pilot?
[13:11] Miguel: Usually 2–4 weeks to provision and test. Private (VPC on your cloud) can be shorter if you already have network infra; if you need we can run a pre-scan.
[13:23] Nina: For evidence collection — will the export contain config.change diffs?
[13:28] Miguel: Yes, config.change events are in the export with before/after fields. We do a schema where small config values are included inline; large blobs are referenced by id.
[13:40] Samira: Ok, last compliance question — do you support retention hold for legal requests?
[13:46] Miguel: We support retention holds via a hold API, which marks items immutable until release. We can emit hold.create and hold.release events in the audit.
[13:56] Avery: Excellent. We're at 35 minutes left? (laugh) We're actually at ~36 minutes elapsed. Let's go through recap and next steps.
[14:05] Miguel: Recap: Miguel to send sample uncompressed audit export + mapping table; action on SAML mapping done; will provide retention config changes to set embeddings to 7 days and transcripts to 48 hours redacted; provide SOC2 mapping and NDA'd report; IP ranges for Dedicated egress; deletion job schema.
[14:26] Samira: Velocis to confirm SCIM needs, list of people who need export rights and timeline for pilot extension decision.
[14:33] Nina: We'll also run a set of token retention tests and report back.
[14:37] Avery: Perfect. Any final questions?
[14:40] Samira: None. Thanks everyone.
[14:43] Tom: Thanks all.
[14:44] Miguel: Thanks, will follow up.
[14:46] Avery: End of meeting.
[14:47] *meeting ended*
